text: The annual report of the Royal Dutch Petroleum Company states that the production of the Royal Dutch group in 1925 amounted to 12,890,000 tons compared with 13,442,000 in 1924, and refers to the remarkable production of the Dutch East Indies Oil Company at Djambi.

label: text
text: It says that new hopes are founded on the Bills submitted to the Dutch East Indies People's Council in December last aiming at the development of oilfields of several thousand acres within the sphere of the Dutch East Indies Oil Company.

label: text
text: The report cites the proposed exploration agreements with the Netherlands Colonial Oil Company, a dependent Company of the Standard Oil Company, as proving that the Royal Dutch Company sincerely advocates the open door policy.

text: The India Office announces that the Government of India has decided to fix ten years as the period within which the export of opium from India, other than for strictly medical purposes, will be progressively and finally extinguished.

label: text
text: Accordingly 10 per cent. reduction in such exports will be effected in 1927. Thus the last export will occur in 1935:

label: text
text: During this period the exports will be under a system of direct sale to the Government importing countries.

text: His Holiness the Pope gave an audience to the Buenos Aires architect, Senior Mario Palanti, who has come to Rome to submit plans for building a skyscraper of 47 storeys intended as a monument to the Fascist regime.

label: text
text: The building will contain an hotel of 3,000 rooms, an audi-torium seating 13,000, Roman baths, and a church which will be the highest in Rome.

Franco-Chinese Institute in Lyons have subscribed 1,100 francs toward the voluntary fund for the redemption of the National Debt.
In a letter to the Director of the Institute the students say that the sum is small but it is proof of their sympathy and gratitude toward France. They recall the Chinese proverb "From one thousand paces one sends a feather. The gift is light, but the friendship is heavy." They conclude: "That is exactly our case."

label: text
text: Questions were asked by Mr. Rumsey MacDonald and by Lord Henry Cavendish Bentinek (Conservative) as to what action the Government proposed to take in view of the failure of Tuesday's conversations between the miners and coal owners.

label: text
text: The Premier replied that the task of making effective the recommendations of the Coal Commission must rest primarily and mainly with the coal industry itself, but the Government, although its proposals had been rejected by the owners and miners, were continuing the preparation of legislative and administrative measures indicated in those proposals. He was "not in a position to make a further statement at the moment. Next Tuesday would be set aside for a discussion on the whole mining question, in whatever form Mr. Ramsay MacDonald might desire it, should take.

text: TRADE OF GREAT VALUE AND MAGNITUDE.

label: text
text: The third report of the Imperial Economic Committee 'contains a numbers of interesting facts and recommendations with reference to the consumption of Empire fruit in this country.

label: text
text: Committee's labours is the setting up of an Empire Marketing Board whose duties will be to carry out the recommendations of the Committee and to spend the £1,000,000 a year which Parliament has voted to assist the marketing of Empire Foodstuffs. The Committee point out that the supply of fruit to this country is a trade of great magnitude and value. More than three quarters of the fruit imports are derived from foreign countries and less than one-quarter from the overseas Empire. It is the deliberate opinion of the Committee that the greater part of the fruit now derived from foreign countries might at no very distant date be obtained from British sources overseas. The result of such expansion of markets in the Home country for Empire fruit would be seen in the corresponding growth of British overseas markets for goods manufactured by the Home country. The Committee considered how the fruit industries of the Empire could best be developed and one policy which seemed to be immediately available was that which they had described in their first report as the policy of developing voluntary preference on the part of the consumer. This policy, it is recommended, should be based on firstly, the organisation of producers within the Empire and, secondly, on the mobilisation of consumers in the Home country. In regard to the marketing of fruit, the Empire Marketing Board will organise and operate a campaign of publicity; provide an intelligence service and undertake the direction, co-ordination, and assistance of research both in the Home country and overseas.

label: text
text:
The Home Secretary was asked in the House of Commons what was the attitude of the Government towards the contributions made to the funds of the Miners' Federation by the Russian Government.
Sir William Joynson Hicks, replying, said that members of the Russian Soviet Government had, during the last two years, made repeated public declarations intimating their desire and intention to interfere with the economical affairs of Great Britain. They had made known their intention to take sides, both in the general strike and in the stoppage of the coal mines. He had been informed in a despatch from Russia of considerable sums of money amounting to some hundreds of thousands of pounds being sent, firstly, for the purposes of the general strike, and, secondly, for the purposes of the Minors' Federation. The whole question was one of much importance and it was now being considered by the British Government. He promised a statement on the subject next Thursday.

text:
Moscow, June 11.
The Soviet Trades Unions have so far contributed 3,626,000 roubles to the Miners' Federation of Great Britain.

label: text
text: It is understood that the British Government has sent the Soviet Government a Note pro-tasting against the Soviet Government offering the Trade Union Congress money during the General Strike, which is regarded as, unjustifiable interference with the internal affairs of Britain.

label: text
text: The Acting Charge d'Affaires at the Soviet Embassy has issued a statement denying the Home Secretary's declaration in the House of Commons that the Soviet Government sent money to Great Britain to support the general strike.

label: text
text: In connection with the Chengtu outrage, a Consular report states that the coolie who attacked Mrs. Sibley was armed with a heavy sword with which he severed her head from her body.

label: text
text: The murderer was mortally shot by some soldiers, and died soon afterwards.

label: text
text: [The previous report from Shanghai dated June 9 stated: — A message from Chengtu dated June 7 says that Mrs. Sibley, wife of the Canadian Methodist Missionary stationed at Junghsien, was murdered in a street in Chengtuth's morning. The assailant attacked her with a big knife. The police, after chase, captured the murderer, but it is not yet clear who he is.]

label: text
text: A last moment deadlock has occurred in the furworkers' strike, owing to the Unions insisting that the workers who returned to work during the strike should be "disciplined."

label: text
text: The Committee of fur workers and employers have reached an agreement, subject to ratification by both sides, granting 10 per cent. increase in wages, the 40 hour week to be increased to 44 hours during the busy season.

label: text
text: It is expected that all employees will return to work in a few days. It is estimated the strike cost the workers and employers $29,000,000 (gold).
